why: Most commands work as written. The builder steps are fine: npm install, npm ci && npm test, chmod. The Check 3 `node --input-type=module -e "…"` quoting and escapes come out as valid JS. The Check 4 `node -e "const p=require(...)"` is valid. The gh commands (`pr view --json body,headRefOid,files`, `pr list --search`, `pr checks`) take valid arguments. The problem is that every verifier command in Checks 1 and 2 uses `$T`, as in `printf ... > $T/clean.jsonl` and `node ... $T/does-not-exist.jsonl >$T/o1`, but no step ever sets it. The brief only says to use a scratch directory "e.g. `mktemp -d`" and never gives `T=$(mktemp -d)`. Run as written, `$T` is empty, so the files go to `/clean.jsonl`, `/o1` and so on at the filesystem root. Those writes may fail, or may clobber files, and the PASS lines that expect `$T/bad.jsonl:3:` don't line up with the intended scratch path. Because these commands depend on a variable no earlier step creates, the brief breaks the criterion.
